steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 (PACE) is the primary statute governing police powers in England and Wales, balancing effective law enforcement with the protection of individual rights | Key Fact: Stop and search under PACE section 1 requires reasonable suspicion that the person has stolen or prohibited articles; the officer must state their name, station and the grounds for the search | Key Fact: Reasonable suspicion must be based on objective factors — it cannot be based solely on a person's race, age or appearance (PACE Code A) | Key Fact: An arrest without warrant under PACE section 24 requires reasonable suspicion that the person is about to commit, is committing or has committed an offence, and the arrest must be necessary
